title: 60 Million Pieces Left China Through One Port — Canton Porcelain | China Travel Expert
description:
For about a century, more than 60 million pieces of Chinese porcelain sailed to Europe — and nearly all of it passed through one city.

Before 1842, Guangzhou (Canton) was the sole legal port for China's foreign trade. Plain white and blue-and-white porcelain was made far inland at Jingdezhen, then shipped to Guangzhou, where local workshops painted it in brilliant gold and rose overglaze enamels. This is Guangcai — Canton porcelain — developed by Guangzhou craftsmen during the Qing dynasty. From the 1740s, European nobles began mailing in their own designs: family coats-of-arms, portraits, even copies of European paintings, which Canton artisans meticulously reproduced onto the glaze. A hand-painted, made-to-order teaset from Guangzhou became one of the most fashionable objects in 18th-century Europe — porcelain designed in China, for the world.

🧭 Expert Tip: To tell real Canton ware, look for the dense gold rim and the pink famille-rose enamel. Guangdong's museums in Guangzhou display fine period pieces up close.
